newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia evaluates licensing of reinsurers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia evaluates licensing of reinsurers.

text.p: The Malaysian government has evaluated several applications for licenses to operate as life reinsurers in Malaysia, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.
He said an announcement will be made at an appropriate time, without giving details.
There have been numerous requests for the opening up of the market, Anwar said at the launch of Malaysian Life Reinsurance Group Bhd (MLRG), the country's first life reinsurance company.
MLRG is 70 percent owned by Life Insurance Association of Malaysia (LIAM) and 30 percent by Reinsurance Group of America.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the insurance industry in Malaysia has tremendous potential.

He said despite the strong growth of the country's economy in the last decade, the market penetration for life insurance coverage remained low, with aggregate sums insured increasing at an average annual rate of 19.8 percent and annual premiums in force growing by 19.2 percent.
"But the number of policies in force only amounts to about 25 percent of the population, or one out of four people," he said.

This was still low by international standards, Anwar said, adding that on average, each Malaysian spends only 218 ringgit on life insurance coverage or two percent of the per capita income of 10,075 ringgit.
LIAM president Ezamshah Ismail said MLRG was fortunate to be able to ride on this potential growth with the experience of an acclaimed life reinsurance specialist.
The company plans to expand beyond Malaysia after three years of operation, he said.
MLRG, which has a paid-up capital of 50 million ringgit, will cover life, health and accident reinsurance.
At present, there are only six branches of reinsurance companies and one reinsurance company handling general reinsurance business in the country.
